I couldn't find Ville's inequality for non-negative (super)martingales in Mathlib. Doob's finite-horizon maximal_ineq is there; I mean the infinite-horizon μ {ω | ∃ n, c ≤ M n ω} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((∫ ω, M 0 ω ∂μ) / c).

We have a proof for non-negative martingales (ville_inequality, plus a supremum form) as part of an anytime-valid change-detection result: https://github.com/jdhart81/viridis-canon/blob/main/series/ACC/PaperFormalization/NullMartingale.lean#L104
It is Lean 4.28 against Mathlib 8f9d9cf and uses only the standard axioms; the change-detection theorem built on it was comparator-checked by the Lean and nanoda kernels (certificates/Run-129 in the same repo). Disclosure: the proof is AI-generated.

Is this already somewhere I missed? If not, would a PR be welcome? I'd generalize it to supermartingales and follow Mathlib style. Pointers on where it should live are appreciated.
